# Drawing Rectangles

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Drawing Rectangles

In Chapter 1 you set up the canvas and learned how the coordinate system works. Now it is time to actually draw something.

The rectangle is the most used shape in Brick Breaker. The paddle is a rectangle. Every brick is a rectangle. Canvas gives you three rectangle methods right out of the box.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3ctx.fillRect(150, 260, 100, 12);
4ctx.fillRect(50, 50, 80, 25);
5ctx.fillRect(140, 50, 80, 25);
6ctx.strokeRect(230, 50, 80, 25);
```

Click Run Code and you will see a paddle near the bottom and a row of bricks near the top.

Here is what each method does:

- fillRect draws a solid filled rectangle
- strokeRect draws just the outline of a rectangle
- clearRect erases everything inside the given area

All three take the same four arguments. x, y, width, and height.

![Canvas showing labeled fillRect and strokeRect shapes](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

clearRect might not feel important right now. But in Chapter 3 it becomes the most used method in the entire game. Every animation frame starts with it.

Next, you will learn how to draw circles, which is how the ball gets drawn in Brick Breaker.
